entries.name: Apache SkyWalking
entries.use_for: Self-hosted APM with distributed tracing and service topology
entries.why: Apache top-level APM with agents for many languages, eBPF profiling and OpenTelemetry ingest.
entries.summary: Open-source APM for distributed systems providing tracing, service topology, metrics and alarming for microservices and cloud-native stacks.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted APM across microservices, with many language agents.
entries.not_for: Large footprint to run; overkill for small apps.

entries.name: CocoaLumberjack
entries.use_for: Fast, flexible logging for Apple platforms
entries.why: Long-standing logging framework for iOS/macOS with file and custom loggers.
entries.summary: Logging framework for Apple platforms (macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS) with multiple loggers such as os_log and file.
entries.best_for: Apps on Apple platforms needing flexible logging.
entries.not_for: Apple platforms only; Apple's unified logging may suffice for simple needs.

entries.name: debug
entries.use_for: Namespaced debug logging for Node and browsers
entries.why: Tiny, ubiquitous debug logger toggled by the DEBUG env var; a dependency of much of npm.
entries.summary: Tiny JavaScript debug logging utility for Node and browsers with namespaces toggled through the DEBUG environment variable.
entries.best_for: Optional namespaced debug output in libraries and Node apps.
entries.not_for: Not a structured production logger.

entries.name: Dozzle
entries.use_for: Realtime web log viewer for Docker, Swarm and K8s containers
entries.why: Lightweight self-hosted container log viewer, widely deployed alongside dev and homelab stacks.
entries.summary: Lightweight web-based real-time log viewer for Docker, Swarm and Kubernetes containers, with fuzzy and regex search; it does not store logs.
entries.best_for: Quickly viewing live container logs.
entries.not_for: No log storage or alerting; not a log aggregation system.

entries.name: Fluentd
entries.use_for: Unified logging layer to collect and route logs
entries.why: CNCF graduated log collector with a large plugin ecosystem.
entries.summary: Log collector providing a unified logging layer that collects events from sources and routes to many outputs via plugins.
entries.best_for: Centralized log routing across diverse systems.
entries.not_for: Ruby-based and heavier than Fluent Bit; plugin management needed.

entries.name: Grafana
entries.use_for: Build dashboards and alerts over Prometheus, Loki, Postgres and dozens of other data sources.
entries.why: The standard observability dashboard (~77k stars, AGPL-3.0); pairs with Prometheus, Loki and Tempo.
entries.summary: Platform to query, visualize and alert on metrics, logs and traces from many data sources, with dashboards and panel plugins.
entries.best_for: Dashboards and alerting over Prometheus, Loki and many databases.
entries.not_for: It stores no data itself; needs data sources.

entries.name: Grafana Loki
entries.use_for: Aggregate and query logs cheaply by indexing only labels.
entries.why: Cost-efficient log store that pairs natively with Grafana and Prometheus labels (AGPL-3.0).
entries.summary: Horizontally scalable multi-tenant log aggregation system that indexes only labels rather than log content, inspired by Prometheus.
entries.best_for: Cost-effective log storage for Kubernetes and Grafana users.
entries.not_for: No full-text indexing, so content search is slower than Elasticsearch.

entries.name: Grafana Pyroscope
entries.use_for: Continuous profiling down to the line of code
entries.why: Grafana's continuous profiling backend with SDKs and eBPF; complements Loki/Tempo; AGPL-3.0.
entries.summary: Continuous profiling platform for CPU, memory and I/O with line-level insight across services.
entries.best_for: Finding performance bottlenecks and cutting resource usage in production.
entries.not_for: Requires profiling agent instrumentation; not for logs or metrics.

entries.name: HyperDX
entries.use_for: Self-host one platform for logs, metrics, traces, errors and session replays.
entries.why: MIT-licensed, OpenTelemetry-native, ClickHouse-backed; now part of ClickStack.
entries.summary: Self-hostable observability on ClickHouse that correlates logs, metrics, traces, errors and session replays, schema agnostic.
entries.best_for: Teams on ClickHouse wanting a unified observability UI.
entries.not_for: Requires ClickHouse infrastructure.

entries.name: Jaeger
entries.use_for: Collect, store and visualize distributed traces.
entries.why: CNCF-graduated tracing backend with native OpenTelemetry ingestion.
entries.summary: Distributed tracing platform to collect, store and visualize traces, with OpenTelemetry support.
entries.best_for: Debugging latency across microservices.
entries.not_for: Traces only, no metrics or logs; storage backend needed at scale.

entries.name: Kubeshark
entries.use_for: Inspect Kubernetes L4/L7 API traffic with full context
entries.why: eBPF-powered traffic observability for K8s, like Wireshark for clusters.
entries.summary: Kubernetes network observability using eBPF to index cluster traffic, offering L4/L7 API inspection, PCAP downloads and visualization.
entries.best_for: Debugging Kubernetes service traffic.
entries.not_for: Kubernetes only and kernel-level access required.

entries.name: Langfuse
entries.use_for: Trace, evaluate and debug LLM apps and agents, with prompt management.
entries.why: Leading open-source LLM observability platform (~36k stars) with SDKs and OTel support.

license_verified.note: MIT outside ee/ directories (those are under ee/LICENSE)

entries.summary: Open-source LLM engineering platform with tracing, evaluation, prompt management, datasets and analytics, self-hostable or cloud.
entries.best_for: Monitoring and evaluating LLM apps and agents.
entries.not_for: Self-hosting needs ClickHouse, Postgres and more; some features require cloud/enterprise.

entries.name: lnav
entries.use_for: Navigate, merge and query log files in the terminal
entries.why: Powerful log file navigator with automatic format detection and SQL queries over logs.
entries.summary: Terminal log file viewer that decompresses, detects formats, merges logs by time, tails files and supports SQL queries.
entries.best_for: Investigating local log files over SSH.
entries.not_for: Terminal tool, not a centralized log platform.

entries.name: logrus
entries.use_for: Structured, pluggable logging for Go
entries.why: Classic Go structured logger with hooks; huge installed base (maintenance mode but stable).
entries.summary: Structured logger for Go compatible with the standard log API. The README states it is in maintenance mode.
entries.best_for: Existing Go projects already using logrus.
entries.not_for: Maintenance mode; new Go projects can use log/slog.

entries.name: Loguru
entries.use_for: Add readable, structured logging to Python apps with almost no setup.
entries.why: Most popular third-party Python logger; one import replaces stdlib logging boilerplate.
entries.summary: Python logging library with simple setup via a single logger object, handlers, rotation, structured output and better exceptions.
entries.best_for: Python apps wanting easy logging with minimal config.
entries.not_for: Not stdlib-compatible out of the box; fewer integrations than logging.

entries.name: Monolog
entries.use_for: PSR-3 logging for PHP with many handlers
entries.why: The standard PHP logger used by Laravel and Symfony.
entries.summary: PSR-3 logging library for PHP that sends logs to files, sockets, databases and web services via handlers.
entries.best_for: PHP apps and frameworks (Laravel, Symfony).
entries.not_for: PHP only; version 3.x needs newer PHP.

entries.name: Netdata
entries.use_for: Monitor servers and containers in real time with per-second metrics and zero config.
entries.why: Very popular infra monitoring agent (~81k stars, GPL-3.0) with auto-discovery of services.
entries.summary: Real-time infrastructure monitoring with per-second metrics, auto-discovery and ML-based anomaly detection with zero config.
entries.best_for: Quick monitoring of servers and containers.
entries.not_for: Agent per node; some features are tied to Netdata Cloud.

entries.name: Nightingale
entries.use_for: Self-hosted alerting and monitoring for metrics, logs and databases
entries.why: CCF open-source monitoring/alerting platform working on top of Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics and more.
entries.summary: Self-hosted alerting engine connecting Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics, Elasticsearch, Loki and ClickHouse with rule management, notification routing and an AI agent.
entries.best_for: Alerting across existing monitoring data sources.
entries.not_for: Alerting-centric; doesn't collect metrics itself, and docs lean Chinese.

entries.name: OpenObserve
entries.use_for: Self-hosted logs, metrics and traces platform on object storage
entries.why: Rust all-in-one observability backend positioned as a low-cost Elasticsearch/Datadog alternative; AGPL-3.0.
entries.summary: Self-hosted observability platform for logs, metrics, traces, RUM and LLM monitoring using object storage, as an alternative to Datadog or Elasticsearch.
entries.best_for: Cost-efficient unified observability at large scale.
entries.not_for: Younger ecosystem than Grafana or Elastic.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry Collector
entries.use_for: Receive, process and export traces, metrics and logs in a vendor-neutral pipeline.
entries.why: CNCF core component (~8k stars) for routing OTel data to any backend.
entries.summary: Vendor-agnostic collector to receive, process and export traces, metrics and logs, replacing multiple agents.
entries.best_for: Central telemetry pipeline routing to multiple backends.
entries.not_for: Needs config and operation; the core distribution has limited components.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry Go
entries.use_for: Instrument Go services with vendor-neutral traces, metrics and logs.
entries.why: Official OpenTelemetry API and SDK for Go; export to any OTel-compatible backend.
entries.summary: Go implementation of OpenTelemetry APIs and SDK, with stable traces, metrics and logs.
entries.best_for: Instrumenting Go services in a vendor-neutral way.
entries.not_for: Instrumentation only; needs a backend, and manual spans needed.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry JS
entries.use_for: Instrument Node.js and browser apps with OpenTelemetry traces and metrics.
entries.why: Official OTel SDK for JavaScript (~3.5k stars); vendor-neutral instrumentation.
entries.summary: JavaScript OpenTelemetry for Node.js and browsers: APIs and SDKs for traces and metrics, with notes on CommonJS vs ESM.
entries.best_for: Instrumenting Node and browser apps.
entries.not_for: Docs assume CommonJS; ESM needs extra setup.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry Python
entries.use_for: Instrument Python apps with OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs.
entries.why: Official OTel SDK for Python; auto-instrumentation for Django, Flask, FastAPI and more.
entries.summary: Python OpenTelemetry API and SDK; traces and metrics are stable, while logs are in development with possible breaking changes.
entries.best_for: Instrumenting Python services vendor-neutrally.
entries.not_for: Logs signal is not yet stable; needs a collector or backend.

entries.name: Pino
entries.use_for: Write fast structured JSON logs from Node.js apps.
entries.why: The fastest mainstream Node.js logger with transports and framework integrations (Fastify default).
entries.summary: Very low-overhead Node.js logger that outputs structured JSON, with child loggers and transports.
entries.best_for: High-throughput Node services needing structured logs.
entries.not_for: JSON output needs pino-pretty for dev; Node/JS only.

entries.name: Prometheus
entries.use_for: Collect and query metrics and alert on them.
entries.why: CNCF-graduated standard for metrics monitoring; the PromQL ecosystem is everywhere.
entries.summary: Monitoring system that scrapes metrics into a time-series database, with PromQL queries and alerting rules.
entries.best_for: Metrics monitoring and alerting for cloud-native services.
entries.not_for: Metrics only, pull-based with limited long-term storage.

entries.name: Sentry JavaScript SDK
entries.use_for: Capture errors, performance traces and replays from browser and Node apps.
entries.why: Official Sentry SDKs (MIT) for React, Next.js, Node and more; the most used error-tracking client.
entries.summary: Official Sentry SDKs for JavaScript under the @sentry/ namespace. They capture errors, performance traces and session replays from browser and Node.js apps, with framework-specific packages and a shared core plus a replay integration.
entries.best_for: Adding error tracking, tracing and session replay to React, Next.js, Node or other JS apps that report to Sentry.
entries.not_for: Only useful with a Sentry backend (hosted or self-hosted); not a standalone logging or metrics tool, and not for backends in other languages.

entries.name: SigNoz
entries.use_for: Self-host an OpenTelemetry-native APM with logs, traces and metrics in one app.
entries.why: Open-source Datadog alternative (~32k stars) built on OTel and ClickHouse.

license_verified.note: MIT outside ee/ and cmd/enterprise/ (those are under ee/LICENSE)

entries.summary: Open-source observability platform built on OpenTelemetry that puts logs, metrics, traces, alerts, dashboards and exceptions in one app. It stores telemetry in a single columnar database and offers APM views for latency, error rate and endpoints.
entries.best_for: Self-hosting a Datadog-style APM on OpenTelemetry with correlated logs, traces and metrics and no per-host pricing.
entries.not_for: You must run and operate the stack yourself (or pay for cloud); overkill if you only need a logger or error tracker. Best with OTel instrumentation.

entries.name: spdlog
entries.use_for: Fast, header-only C++ logging
entries.why: The default C++ logging library: fmt-based, async sinks, very fast.

license_verified.note: LICENSE file is the MIT License

entries.summary: Fast C++ logging library, usable header-only or as a compiled library. Supports multiple platforms (Linux, Windows, macOS, Android, BSDs) and is available through most package managers.
entries.best_for: C++11+ projects needing a fast, ready-made logger with sinks and async logging that is easy to install via vcpkg, apt or Homebrew.
entries.not_for: C++ only. Not a log aggregation or observability backend; header-only mode increases compile times (compiled version recommended).

entries.name: Telegraf
entries.use_for: Collect and ship metrics/logs from 300+ sources
entries.why: Plugin-driven collection agent with input/output plugins for nearly every system; 1,500+ contributors.
entries.summary: Plugin-driven agent for collecting, processing, aggregating and writing metrics, logs and other data. It ships 300+ input and output plugins, compiles to a static binary with no dependencies and is configured via TOML.
entries.best_for: Collecting system, cloud, device and messaging metrics on hosts and shipping them to InfluxDB, Prometheus or other backends.
entries.not_for: It is only a collection agent, with no storage, querying or dashboards of its own; use another tool for full pipeline routing or for in-app instrumentation.

entries.name: Thanos
entries.use_for: Highly available Prometheus with long-term object storage
entries.why: CNCF project adding global query, HA and unlimited retention to Prometheus.
entries.summary: Set of components that sit on top of existing Prometheus deployments to add high availability, a global query view and unlimited retention. It uses the Prometheus 2.0 storage format to keep historical data in object storage.
entries.best_for: Prometheus users who need long-term storage in S3/GCS-style object storage, global querying across clusters and HA.
entries.not_for: More moving parts than plain Prometheus; not worth it for a single small Prometheus. It extends Prometheus rather than replacing it.

entries.name: Timber
entries.use_for: Extensible logging API for Android
entries.why: The standard Android logging wrapper on top of Android's Log class.
entries.summary: Small, extensible logger for Android that wraps the standard Log class. Behavior is added by planting Tree instances (e.g. DebugTree, which auto-tags with the calling class) and it ships with lint rules.
entries.best_for: Android apps that want simple tagged debug logging and pluggable production logging (e.g. crash reporting trees).
entries.not_for: Android only. No log shipping or aggregation; you write your own Tree for production destinations.

entries.name: tracing
entries.use_for: Instrument Rust apps with structured, async-aware spans and events.
entries.why: The standard Rust instrumentation framework, with OpenTelemetry and log subscribers.
entries.summary: Instrumentation framework for Rust that records structured, async-aware spans and events. Subscribers handle output, with integrations for logging and OpenTelemetry.
entries.best_for: Rust services, especially async/Tokio code, needing structured diagnostics, spans and trace export.
entries.not_for: Rust only. It is an instrumentation API and needs a subscriber/exporter plus a separate backend to store and view data.

entries.name: Vector
entries.use_for: Collect, transform and route logs and metrics to any backend.
entries.why: High-performance Rust observability pipeline from Datadog; replaces Logstash/Fluentd setups.
entries.summary: High-performance observability data pipeline written in Rust that acts as agent and aggregator. It collects, transforms and routes logs and metrics from sources to any sinks, vendor-neutral.
entries.best_for: Replacing Logstash/Fluentd-style shippers, routing telemetry to multiple vendors and cutting observability costs through filtering and enrichment.
entries.not_for: A pipeline only, with no storage or UI; configuration has a learning curve and it is overkill for a single app writing logs to one place.

entries.name: VictoriaMetrics
entries.use_for: Store and query metrics at scale as a Prometheus-compatible backend.
entries.why: Drop-in Prometheus long-term storage with lower resource use; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Time-series database and monitoring backend that is Prometheus-compatible. Available as a single-node version and a cluster version under Apache-2.0, aimed at low resource use and scale.
entries.best_for: Long-term, high-volume metrics storage as a drop-in Prometheus remote-write/query backend with lower resource use.
entries.not_for: Metrics-focused; for logs and traces you need other tools. Enterprise features and support are commercial.

entries.name: winston
entries.use_for: Log from Node.js with multiple transports, levels and formats.
entries.why: Long-standing Node logger (~27M weekly npm downloads) with a large transport ecosystem.
entries.summary: Logger for Node.js with multiple transports, log levels and formats. You create loggers with createLogger and route different levels to files, console or other transports.
entries.best_for: Node.js apps needing flexible logging to several destinations with a large ecosystem of community transports.
entries.not_for: Node.js only. Slower than newer loggers such as pino for very high throughput; log aggregation is left to external transports.

entries.name: zap
entries.use_for: Write fast, structured, leveled logs in Go.
entries.why: Uber's zero-allocation structured logger; one of the most used Go logging libraries.
entries.summary: Structured, leveled logging library for Go. Offers a strongly typed Logger with minimal allocations and a SugaredLogger with a looser printf-style API.
entries.best_for: Go services where logging performance matters, with typed fields and JSON output in production.
entries.not_for: Go only. The typed API is more verbose; for simple needs the standard log/slog may be enough. It does not ship logs anywhere.

entries.name: zerolog
entries.use_for: Zero-allocation JSON logging for Go
entries.why: One of the fastest Go structured loggers with a chainable API.
entries.summary: Zero-allocation JSON logger for Go with a chainable API. It focuses on structured logging only, supports levels, sampling, hooks, context integration and log/slog, plus a ConsoleWriter for development.
entries.best_for: Go projects wanting very fast structured JSON (or CBOR) logs with a fluent API and context.Context integration.
entries.not_for: Go only and JSON-first; the pretty console writer is slow and meant for dev. Not a log transport or backend.

entries.name: Zipkin
entries.use_for: Collect and view distributed traces
entries.why: Long-standing distributed tracing system and UI; compatible with OpenTelemetry exporters.
entries.summary: Distributed tracing system that collects and looks up timing data to troubleshoot latency in service architectures. It offers a UI for searching traces and a dependency diagram, and apps report via HTTP, Kafka and other transports.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted tracing backend and UI for microservices, including via OpenTelemetry-compatible exporters.
entries.not_for: Tracing only (no logs or metrics); applications must be instrumented. Heavier alternatives like Jaeger/Tempo or SigNoz cover more.
